lots.what_it_is: Pair of turquoise ribbed glass vases with ruffled amethyst rims, applied green vines and leaves, applied clear and amber berries, and gilt and enamel flowers. Gowans calls them 'Venetian style', but the decoration is Bohemian enamelled and applied glass, in the manner of Harrach, Moser or Heckert, late 19th century or a later copy.
lots.guide_summary: Nothing survives: 0 sold, 0 unsold, 0 asking. The researcher found no entries because the shared web search budget had run out, and it was still used up when I checked, so I could not add any. Any value figure here would be a guess.
lots.working: No SOLD evidence, so there is no basis for a maximum bid. keep_max_hammer = 0, flip_max_hammer = 0.
lots.confidence_reason: There is only one photo, the bases are not shown, no maker's mark can be read and there is no price evidence of any kind.
lots.key_photo_findings: One photo of the pair. Enlarged crops show the applied leaves, stems and berries are thick, lumpy hot-worked glass with gilt highlights, plus hand-gilt sprigs and raised enamel flowers and berries. This fits Bohemian work of about 1880 to 1900, but well-made later copies exist. The right vase has a flat, dark grey, leaf-shaped patch with a pale edge high on its right side. It could be a dark enamel leaf, a reflection or a repair, and I can't tell which. The lower inside of the right vase looks cloudy or stained (possibly 'sick' glass or dried water residue). Applied berries are the usual weak point, and none look obviously missing, but small chips can't be ruled out. No lot description and no measurements.
lots.condition: Unknown from one photo. Possible cloudy interior on the right vase, an unexplained dark patch on the right vase, and rims, feet and applied decoration not checked for chips or losses.
lots.question_for_gowans: Please check: (1) the height of each vase; (2) the bases for a ground pontil, wear and any mark or number; (3) whether the inside of the right vase is cloudy or etched rather than just dirty; (4) what the dark grey leaf-shaped patch high on the right vase is (enamel, repair or damage); (5) any chips, cracks or missing applied berries or leaves, and any rim damage.
lots.score_reason: If they are genuine 19th century Bohemian enamelled and applied glass, a matched pair could be worth a few hundred dollars. I've discounted heavily for the unconfirmed period, the possibility of reproduction, the possibly cloudy interior and the complete lack of price evidence.
